dataset.name: EgoOops
dataset.license_or_access_note: Official EgoOops video, CC BY-SA 4.0. Same locally acquired original recording; only source provenance is reused from the prior candidate.

observed_events.description: The wearer points the short cylindrical hand light at nearby cups. Its purple beam produces colored fluorescence; the same lamp remains in use.
The light is put down near the box. The wearer later picks up and tilts two small sample cups.

screening.proposed_instruction: Could you put one like this in my cart?
screening.source_continuity: Continuous 188–219 s, with a one-time opening utterance and no wait cut.

supported_claims.text: The left hand holds a short handheld light producing UV fluorescence on nearby samples.
The flashlight is set aside and the wearer turns to holding and tilting two small cups. The item requested at opening is unchanged.

construct.research_question: Does an agent retain the visually grounded shopping target after the wearer puts down the requested tool and handles a different item?
construct.belief_before: The handheld lamp projects purple light and causes nearby samples to fluoresce. The request refers to that lamp.
construct.belief_after: The wearer sets the lamp down and handles sample cups. The original request remains anchored to the lamp.
construct.required_behavior_change: Keep or select one eligible handheld UV light. Do not replace it with a cup or add a second listing.
construct.no_update_failure: Choose a conventional work light, fixed fixture or otherwise unsupported tool rather than the initially identified handheld UV light.
construct.overupdate_failure: Remove an already valid UV lamp and replace it with a cup, or retain both products.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The opening request says only this. A compact blacklight, ordinary inspection lights and cups all occur in the site, while the held lamp and its effect distinguish the requested product.

task_blueprint.instruction: Could you put one like this in my cart?

observed.why: The left hand holds and aims the light as the wearer refers to it.
The later sample cups change the visible activity, not the referent of the already expressed request.
